> display.dev is the easiest way to publish agent-generated artifacts behind company authentication. One command gives your HTML and Markdown files a permanent URL. Your colleagues sign in securely via OTP or Google/Microsoft SSO, and drive iteration with in-line comments.

## Content

display.dev is a gated publishing layer for the artifacts that AI agents now produce every day: HTML reports, Markdown documents, dashboards, specs, prototypes, and review pages. Instead of sending screenshots or raw files, teams publish one permanent URL behind company authentication.

## What problem does display.dev solve?

The official display.dev site starts from a practical failure mode: agents can generate rich HTML and Markdown, but sharing those outputs inside a company is clumsy. Screenshots remove interactivity, file uploads confuse nontechnical recipients, and public deploys are wrong for sensitive work. display.dev turns a local artifact into a hosted URL that colleagues can open after signing in with OTP, Google, or Microsoft.

## README

 
 
 

 
 A report inbox for AI agents. 
 Agents publish HTML; you browse and share it over your private network — never the public internet.
 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/009fdad6-5c3d-4f19-b972-db8547a2e27f

## What is this?

Hub is a tiny self-hosted app that collects HTML reports your AI agents write — architecture notes, data reviews, postmortems, anything worth keeping.

You get a clean, Obsidian-style dashboard: a **folder tree** of reports on the left, a **live preview** on the right. Reports carry a summary and an optional link (PR/issue) that Hub badges with the right icon. Everything is reachable only on your private network (a Tailscale tailnet or a company VPN), never the public internet. Run it just for yourself, or host **one shared instance** your whole team publishes to and reads from.

```mermaid
  B --> C[Dashboard]
  B -->|private network| D[Teammates]
```
